types:** `visitor_entered`, `visitor_exited`, `vehicle_entered`, `vehicle_exited`, `disinfection_completed`, `disinfection_missed`, `health_incident`, `vaccination_recorded`, `animal_movement`, `inspection_completed`, `feed_delivery`, `restricted_zone_entry`, `sanitation_completed`\n\n---\n\n## 8. API Integration Points (Existing Service Layer)\n\nAll integration should target `src/services/api.ts`. Current service methods:\n\n```typescript\n// farmService\ngetFarm(farmId: string): Promise<Farm>\ngetAllFarms(): Promise<Farm[]>\n\n// passportService\ngetBiosecurityPassport(farmId: string): Promise<BiosecurityPassport>\n\n// incidentService\ngetIncidents(farmId?: string): Promise<IncidentReport[]>\nsubmitIncident(payload): Promise<IncidentReport>\nverifyIncident(incidentId, action, notes?): Promise<IncidentReport>\n\n// correctiveActionService\ngetActions(farmId?: string): Promise<CorrectiveAction[]>\nsubmitEvidence(actionId, evidence): Promise<CorrectiveAction>\nverifyAction(actionId, approved: boolean): Promise<CorrectiveAction>\n\n// riskService\ngetRiskFactors(): Promise<RiskFactor[]>\n\n// gisService\ngetGisMapNodes(): Promise<GisMapNode[]>\n\n// officerService\ngetOfficerStats(): Promise<OfficerStats>\n\n// notificationService\ngetNotifications(role?: UserRole): Promise<NotificationItem[]>\nmarkAsRead(id: string): Promise<void>\n```\n\n### Components → Service Call Map\n\n| Component | Service Methods |\n|-----------|----------------|\n| `AuthContext` | *(currently mockData — needs auth + farm list API)* |\n| `BiosecurityPassportModal` | `passportService.getBiosecurityPassport` |\n| `IncidentReportForm` | `incidentService.submitIncident` |\n| `VetDashboard` | `incidentService.getIncidents`, `verifyIncident` |\n| `CorrectiveActionsList` | `correctiveActionService.getActions`, `verifyAction` |\n| `EvidenceUploadModal` | `correctiveActionService.submitEvidence` |\n| `RiskDashboard` | `riskService.getRiskFactors` |\n| `OfficerDashboard` | `officerService.getOfficerStats`, `farmService.getAllFarms` |\n| `GisFarmMap` | `gisService.getGisMapNodes` |\n| `NotificationContext` | `notificationService.getNotifications`, `markAsRead` |\n| `FarmerDashboard` | *(simulation snapshot — separate integration path)* |\n\n---\n\n## 9. Core Workflow Mapping\n\n```\nFarm Registration → Biosecurity Assessment → Risk Calculation → Incident Reporting\n→ GIS/Spatial Risk Analysis → Veterinary Verification → Corrective Action Generation\n→ Farmer Action Completion → Evidence Upload → Veterinary Verification\n→ Compliance Closure → Risk Recalculation\n```\n\n| Workflow Step | Frontend Support | Backend Responsibility | Trigger |\n|---------------|------------------|------------------------|---------|\n| **Farm Registration** | Farm selector shows registered farms; no registration UI | Create farm record, assign owner, store coordinates | Admin/officer API (no UI yet) |\n| **Biosecurity Assessment** | Passport displays component scores | Assessment questionnaire scoring engine | On registration + periodic reassessment |\n| **Risk Calculation** | RiskDashboard factors; simulation live scoring; passport score | Risk engine: factors, history, spatial weighting | Continuous + on events |\n| **Incident Reporting** | `IncidentReportForm` | Store incident, notify vet/officer, bump risk | Farmer submits form |\n| **GIS/Spatial Risk Analysis** | `GisFarmMap` with filters | Geo queries, proximity risk, containment zones | Officer/vet views map |\n| **Veterinary Verification** | `VetDashboard` | Validate/reject/request-info; audit trail | Vet action buttons |\n| **Corrective Action Generation** | Actions appear in list (mock seeded) | Auto-generate from verified incidents + risk rules | Backend on incident verify / risk threshold |\n| **Farmer Action Completion** | Checklist toggle (local only today) | Track checklist completion | Farmer updates |\n| **Evidence Upload** | `EvidenceUploadModal` | File storage + metadata | Farmer submits evidence |\n| **Veterinary Verification (evidence)** | Verify/Reject in Actions table | Approve/reject evidence | Vet/officer buttons |\n| **Compliance Closure** | Action status → `Verified`/`Closed` | Close workflow, update passport compliance | Backend state machine |\n| **Risk Recalculation** | Simulation + static chart | Recalculate farm/district scores | After each workflow transition |\n\n---\n\n## 10. Authentication & Authorization\n\n### 10.1 Current State (Demo Mode)\n\n- **No login screen**, no tokens, no sessions\n- Role selected via Navbar toggle (`farmer` | `veterinarian` | `officer`)\n- Farm selected via dropdown from `allFarmsMock`\n- Any role can view any tab (sidebar hides `officer` tab for farmer only)\n\n### 10.2 Required Authentication (Production)\n\n| Requirement | Recommendation |\n|-------------|----------------|\n| **Auth method** | JWT (access + refresh) or session cookie |\n| **Login** | Email/phone + password; optional OTP for farmers |\n| **Token storage** | `httpOnly` cookie (preferred) or `Authorization: Bearer` header |\n| **Role claim** | JWT payload: `{ sub, role, farmIds[], districtId? }` |\n| **Farm scoping** | Farmers restricted to owned/assigned `farmId`(s) |\n| **Vet scoping** | District/region-based incident + action access |\n| **Officer scoping** | Regional read-all; write on inspections/compliance |\n\n### 10.3 Suggested Auth Endpoints\n\nSee [Section 13.1](#131-authentication--users).\n\n### 10.4 Frontend Auth Changes (Non-UI)\n\n- Extend `AuthContext` with `user`, `token`, `login()`, `logout()`, `isAuthenticated`\n- Replace Navbar role switcher with authenticated user role (keep switcher only in dev via env flag)\n- Attach auth header in `api.ts` HTTP client\n- Redirect unauthenticated users (new route or modal — minimal addition)\n\n---\n\n## 11. API Endpoint Specification\n\n**Base URL:** `{VITE_API_BASE_URL}/api/v1`  \n**Content-Type:** `application/json` (unless multipart noted)  \n**Auth header:** `Authorization: Bearer {access_token}`\n\n### 13.1 Authentication & Users\n\n#### `POST /auth/login`\n**Auth:** Public\n\n**Request:**\n```json\n{\n  \"email\": \"rajesh.kumar@example.com\",\n  \"password\": \"securePassword123\"\n}\n```\n\n**Response `200`:**\n```json\n{\n  \"accessToken\": \"eyJhbG...\",\n  \"refreshToken\": \"eyJhbG...\",\n  \"expiresIn\": 3600,\n  \"user\": {\n    \"id\": \"usr-uuid-001\",\n    \"fullName\": \"Rajesh Kumar\",\n    \"email\": \"rajesh.kumar@example.com\",\n    \"role\": \"farmer\",\n    \"farmIds\": [\"FARM-JH-2026-0487\"],\n    \"districtId\": \"district-ranchi\"\n  }\n}\n```\n\n#### `POST /auth/refresh`\n**Request:** `{ \"refreshToken\": \"...\" }`  \n**Response `200`:** `{ \"accessToken\": \"...\", \"expiresIn\": 3600 }`\n\n#### `POST /auth/logout`\n**Auth:** Required — invalidates refresh token.\n\n#### `GET /auth/me`\n**Response `200`:** Same `user` object as login.\n\n---\n\n### 13.2 Farms\n\n#### `GET /farms`\n**Roles:** `veterinarian`, `officer` (all in district/region); `farmer` (own only)\n\n**Query params:** `?districtId=&riskLevel=&farmType=&page=&limit=`\n\n**Response `200`:**\n```json\n{\n  \"data\": [\n    {\n      \"id\": \"FARM-JH-2026-0487\",\n      \"name\": \"GreenValley Bio-Farm #04\",\n      \"location\": \"Ranchi District, Jharkhand\",\n      \"owner\": \"Rajesh Kumar\",\n      \"farmType\": \"poultry\",\n      \"capacity\": 3500,\n      \"animalCount\": 2850,\n      \"biosecurityScore\": 78,\n      \"previousScore\": 74,\n      \"riskLevel\": \"safe\",\n      \"visitorsToday\": 8,\n      \"vehiclesToday\": 4,\n      \"complianceRate\": 88,\n      \"vaccinationCoverage\": 94,\n      \"activeIncidents\": 1,\n      \"activeAlerts\": 2,\n      \"updatedAt\": \"2026-08-11T06:59:00.000Z\",\n      \"coordinates\": { \"lat\": 23.3441, \"lng\": 85.3096 }\n    }\n  ],\n  \"pagination\": { \"page\": 1, \"limit\": 20, \"total\": 142 }\n}\n```\n\n*Matches frontend `Farm` interface exactly.*\n\n#### `GET /farms/:farmId`\n**Roles:** Scoped access  \n**Response `200`:** Single `Farm` object.\n\n#### `POST /farms` *(Registration — no UI yet)*\n**Roles:** `officer`, `farmer` (self-registration if enabled)\n\n**Request:**\n```json\n{\n  \"name\": \"GreenValley Bio-Farm #04\",\n  \"location\": \"Block B, Sector 4, Ranchi District, JH\",\n  \"farmType\": \"poultry\",\n  \"capacity\": 3500,\n  \"animalCount\": 2850,\n  \"coordinates\": { \"lat\": 23.3441, \"lng\": 85.3096 },\n  \"ownerName\": \"Rajesh Kumar\",\n  \"ownerEmail\": \"rajesh.kumar@example.com\",\n  \"ownerPhone\": \"+919876543210\"\n}\n```\n\n**Response `201`:** Created `Farm` + triggers biosecurity assessment job.\n\n#### `PATCH /farms/:farmId`\n**Roles:** `officer`, farm owner  \n**Request:** Partial `Farm` fields (capacity, animalCount, etc.)\n\n---\n\n### 13.3 Biosecurity Passport & Assessment\n\n#### `GET /farms/:farmId/passport`\n**Used by:** `passportService.getBiosecurityPassport`\n\n**Response `200`:**\n```json\n{\n  \"farmId\": \"FARM-JH-2026-0487\",\n  \"farmName\": \"GreenValley Bio-Farm #04\",\n  \"farmType\": \"poultry\",\n  \"ownerName\": \"Rajesh Kumar\",\n  \"location\": \"Block B, Sector 4, Ranchi District, JH\",\n  \"capacity\": 3500,\n  \"animalCount\": 2850,\n  \"biosecurityScore\": 78,\n  \"hygieneScore\": 84,\n  \"visitorControlScore\": 79,\n  \"quarantineProtocolScore\": 85,\n  \"vaccinationCoverage\": 94,\n  \"wasteManagementScore\": 70,\n  \"lastInspectionDate\": \"2026-08-01\",\n  \"inspectionHistory\": [\n    {\n      \"id\": \"INSP-2026-08\",\n      \"date\": \"2026-08-01\",\n      \"inspectorName\": \"Dr. A. K. Sharma (District Vet Officer)\",\n      \"result\": \"Passed\",\n      \"notes\": \"Shed sanitation and perimeter fencing fully compliant.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"complianceStatus\": \"Compliant\",\n  \"riskTrend\": \"improving\",\n  \"passportQrCode\": \"BS-PASSPORT-JH26-0487-VERIFIED\",\n  \"issueDate\": \"2026-01-15\"\n}\n```\n\n*Matches frontend `BiosecurityPassport` interface exactly.*\n\n#### `POST /farms/:farmId/assessments` *(Biosecurity Assessment — backend-only trigger for now)*\n**Request:**\n```json\n{\n  \"responses\": [\n    { \"questionId\": \"Q001\", \"answer\": \"yes\", \"score\": 10 },\n    { \"questionId\": \"Q002\", \"answer\": \"partial\", \"score\": 5 }\n  ],\n  \"assessedBy\": \"usr-uuid-vet-001\"\n}\n```\n\n**Response `201`:**\n```json\n{\n  \"assessmentId\": \"ASSESS-2026-001\",\n  \"farmId\": \"FARM-JH-2026-0487\",\n  \"overallScore\": 78,\n  \"componentScores\": {\n    \"hygiene\": 84,\n    \"visitorControl\": 79,\n    \"quarantineProtocol\": 85,\n    \"wasteManagement\": 70\n  },\n  \"passportUpdated\": true\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n### 13.4 Incidents\n\n#### `GET /incidents`\n**Used by:** `incidentService.getIncidents(farmId?)`\n\n**Query:** `?farmId=FARM-JH-2026-0487&status=&severity=`\n\n**Roles:** Farmer (own farm); Vet/Officer (district)\n\n**Response `200`:**\n```json\n{\n  \"data\": [\n    {\n      \"id\": \"INC-2026-881\",\n      \"farmId\": \"FARM-JH-2026-0102\",\n      \"farmName\": \"Apex Swine Breeding Center\",\n      \"farmType\": \"pig\",\n      \"incidentType\": \"Sudden High Mortality\",\n      \"animalType\": \"Pig (Growers)\",\n      \"numberAffected\": 18,\n      \"dateTime\": \"2026-08-10T14:30:00.000Z\",\n      \"description\": \"Sudden high fever and respiratory distress...\",\n      \"location\": \"Shed 02 - Isolation Ward\",\n      \"evidenceFiles\": [\n        {\n          \"name\": \"lesions_obs_01.jpeg\",\n          \"url\": \"https://storage.example.com/evidence/abc.jpeg\",\n          \"timestamp\": \"2026-08-10T14:35:00.000Z\"\n        }\n      ],\n      \"status\": \"Under Review\",\n      \"severity\": \"critical\",\n      \"veterinarianNotes\": \"Awaiting swab laboratory report.\",\n      \"requestedInfoNotes\": null,\n      \"verifiedAt\": null,\n      \"verifiedBy\": null\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n*Matches frontend `IncidentReport` interface.*\n\n#### `GET /incidents/:incidentId`\n**Response `200`:** Single `IncidentReport`.\n\n#### `POST /incidents`\n**Used by:** `incidentService.submitIncident`  \n**Content-Type:** `multipart/form-data` (if files) OR JSON + separate upload\n\n**JSON Request (without files):**\n```json\n{\n  \"farmId\": \"FARM-JH-2026-0487\",\n  \"incidentType\": \"Sudden Mortality Increase\",\n  \"animalType\": \"Poultry (Broilers)\",\n  \"numberAffected\": 12,\n  \"dateTime\": \"2026-08-11T08:15:00.000Z\",\n  \"description\": \"Observed health anomaly requiring veterinary inspection.\",\n  \"location\": \"Shed 02 - Isolation Pen B\"\n}\n```\n\n**Response `201`:**\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": \"INC-2026-882\",\n  \"farmId\": \"FARM-JH-2026-0487\",\n  \"farmName\": \"GreenValley Bio-Farm #04\",\n  \"farmType\": \"poultry\",\n  \"incidentType\": \"Sudden Mortality Increase\",\n  \"animalType\": \"Poultry (Broilers)\",\n  \"numberAffected\": 12,\n  \"dateTime\": \"2026-08-11T08:15:00.000Z\",\n  \"description\": \"Observed health anomaly...\",\n  \"location\": \"Shed 02 - Isolation Pen B\",\n  \"evidenceFiles\": [],\n  \"status\": \"Reported\",\n  \"severity\": \"medium\"\n}\n```\n\n**Backend side-effects:**\n1. Notify veterinarians (`targetRole: \"veterinarian\"`)\n2. Notify officers if severity ≥ `high`\n3. Recalculate farm risk score\n4. Optionally auto-create corrective action draft\n\n#### `POST /incidents/:incidentId/evidence`\n**Content-Type:** `multipart/form-data`  \n**Body:** `files[]`  \n**Response `201`:** Updated `evidenceFiles` array.\n\n#### `POST /incidents/:incidentId/verify`\n**Used by:** `incidentService.verifyIncident(incidentId, action, notes)`\n\n**Request:**\n```json\n{\n  \"action\": \"validate\",\n  \"notes\": \"Verified by certified District Veterinary Officer. Quarantine boundary activated.\"\n}\n```\n\n`action` enum: `\"validate\"` | `\"request_info\"` | `\"reject\"`\n\n**Response `200`:**\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": \"INC-2026-881\",\n  \"status\": \"Verified\",\n  \"veterinarianNotes\": \"Verified by certified District Veterinary Officer.\",\n  \"verifiedAt\": \"2026-08-11T07:30:00.000Z\",\n  \"verifiedBy\": \"Dr. A. K. Sharma (Vet Officer)\"\n}\n```\n\n**Status mapping:**\n| action | Resulting status |\n|--------|------------------|\n| `validate` | `Verified` |\n| `request_info` | `More Info Required` |\n| `reject` | `Rejected` |\n\n**Backend side-effects on `validate`:**\n- Generate corrective actions\n- Update risk factors\n- Notify farmer\n- Update GIS spatial risk if applicable\n\n---\n\n### 13.5 Corrective Actions\n\n#### `GET /corrective-actions`\n**Used by:** `correctiveActionService.getActions(farmId?)`\n\n**Query:** `?farmId=&status=&priority=`\n\n**Response `200`:**\n```json\n{\n  \"data\": [\n ### Key findings

1. **No real authentication** — role switcher in Navbar is demo-only; no login screen.
2. **All API data is mocked** in `src/data/mockData.ts` + in-memory stores in `api.ts`.
3. **Separate simulation engine** drives live telemetry (events, risk score, Aarohi advisor) — not part of `api.ts`.
4. **File uploads are fake** — only filenames stored; URLs are `"#"`.

### Required backend scope (documented in detail)

- **~35 API endpoints** across auth, farms, passport, incidents, corrective actions, risk, GIS, officer stats, inspections, notifications, telemetry
- **15+ database entities** with ER relationships
- **3 roles:** `farmer`, `veterinarian`, `officer`
- **Request/response schemas** aligned to `src/types/index.ts`

### Integration approach (non-UI changes only)

1. Replace mock implementations in `src/services/api.ts` with HTTP calls
2. Extend `AuthContext` for JWT auth
3. Wire file uploads as `multipart/form-data`
4. Feed hardcoded charts/context from new risk history and spatial-risk endpoints
5. Optionally replace simulation with WebSocket telemetry in production

- 🔧 **Write** — `contents`="from datetime import datetime, timezone\nimport math\nimport uuid\n\nfrom app.models.enums import IncidentSeverity, IncidentStatus, RiskLevel\n\n\ndef generate_id(prefix: str, year: int | None = None) -> str:\n    year = year or datetime.now(timezone.utc).year\n    suffix = uuid.uuid4().hex[:6].upper()\n    return f\"{prefix}-{year}-{suffix}\"\n\n\ndef farm_risk_level(score: int) -> RiskLevel:\n    if score >= 70:\n        return RiskLevel.SAFE\n    if score >= 40:\n        return RiskLevel.CAUTION\n    return RiskLevel.CRITICAL\n\n\ndef clamp_score(value: int) -> int:\n    return max(0, min(100, value))\n\n\ndef incident_severity(number_affected: int) -> IncidentSeverity:\n    if number_affected > 50:\n        return IncidentSeverity.CRITICAL\n    if number_affected > 20:\n        return IncidentSeverity.HIGH\n    if number_affected > 5:\n        return IncidentSeverity.MEDIUM\n    return IncidentSeverity.LOW\n\n\ndef haversine_km(lat1: float, lng1: float, lat2: float, lng2: float) -> float:\n    r = 6371.0\n    p1, p2 = math.radians(lat1), math.radians(lat2)\n    dlat = math.radians(lat2 - lat1)\n    dlng = math.radians(lng2 - lng1)\n    a = math.sin(dlat / 2) ** 2 + math.cos(p1) * math.cos(p2) * math.sin(dlng / 2) ** 2\n    return 2 * r * math.asin(math.sqrt(a))\n\n\ndef format_relative_time(dt: datetime) -> str:\n    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)\n    if dt.tzinfo is None:\n        dt = dt.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)\n    delta = now - dt\n    seconds = int(delta.total_seconds())\n    if seconds < 60:\n        return \"Just now\"\n    minutes = seconds // 60\n    if minutes < 60:\n        return f\"{minutes} mins ago\"\n    hours = minutes // 60\n    if hours < 24:\n        return f\"{hours} hours ago\"\n    days = hours // 24\n    return f\"{days} days ago\"\n\n\nOPEN_INCIDENT_STATUSES = {\n    IncidentStatus.REPORTED,\n    IncidentStatus.UNDER_REVIEW,\n    IncidentStatus.MORE_INFO_REQUIRED,\n}\n\nOPEN_ACTION_STATUSES = {\n    \"Pending\",\n    \"In Progress\",\n    \"Evidence Submitted\",\n    \"Awaiting Verification\",\n}\n", `path`="C:\\Users\\ullas\\Downloads\\FARM-PLATFORM--main\\FARM-PLATFORM--main\\backend\\app\\utils\\helpers.py"

      ])\n        ).scalar() or 0\n\n        return {\n            \"totalRegisteredFarms\": total,\n            \"highRiskFarms\": high,\n            \"mediumRiskFarms\": medium,\n The BioShield backend is in place under `backend/`, aligned with `BACKEND_INTEGRATION_PLAN.md`. The frontend UI was not redesigned; only the service layer was wired to real APIs.

## What was built

### Backend structure (`backend/app/`)
| Layer | Contents |
|-------|----------|
| **core/** | Config, JWT security, RBAC dependencies, error types |
| **models/** | 15+ SQLAlchemy entities (users, farms, incidents, actions, risk, GIS, etc.) |
| **schemas/** | Pydantic models with camelCase JSON for the frontend |
| **services/** | Business logic for all 15 required modules |
| **routers/** | REST endpoints under `/api/v1` |
| **middleware/** | Standardized error responses |
| **utils/** | ID generation, geo distance, serializers |

### Implemented modules
1. Authentication (JWT login/register/refresh/me)
2. User management
3. Farm management (CRUD + registration)
4. Biosecurity assessments → passport scores
5. Health records
6. Risk engine (factors, history, recalculation)
7. Incident reporting
8. Veterinary verification
9. Corrective actions
10. Evidence management (file upload + metadata)
11. Compliance verification (action closure → passport update)
12. Notifications
13. GIS/spatial analysis
14. Officer dashboard stats
15. Inspection scheduling & prioritization

### Other files
- `alembic/versions/001_initial_schema.py` — PostgreSQL migration
- `scripts/seed.py` — demo data only (separate from production logic)
- `docker-compose.yml` — PostgreSQL 16
- `backend/README.md` — setup guide
- `.env.example` for backend and frontend

### Frontend integration (service layer only)
- `src/services/api.ts` — calls real REST APIs instead of mocks
- `src/context/AuthContext.tsx` — loads farms from `GET /api/v1/farms` (falls back to mock if backend is down)

---

## How to run

### 1. Start PostgreSQL
```powershell
cd backend
docker compose up -d
```
*(Docker was not available in this environment — run this on your machine.)*

### 2. Backend setup
```powershell
cd backend
copy .env.example .env
python -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
alembic upgrade head
python -m scripts.seed
uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000
```

### 3. Frontend
```powershell
copy .env.example .env
npm run dev
```

- **API docs:** http://localhost:8000/docs  
- **Health:** http://localhost:8000/health  

### Demo credentials (after seed)
| Role | Email | Password |
|------|-------|----------|
| Farmer | `farmer@bioshield.local` | `farmer123` |
| Veterinarian | `vet@bioshield.local` | `vet123` |
| Officer | `officer@bioshield.local` | `officer123` |

---

## API endpoints (frontend-compatible)

| Service | Endpoint |
|---------|----------|
| Farms | `GET/POST /api/v1/farms` |
| Passport | `GET /api/v1/farms/{id}/passport` |
| Incidents | `GET/POST /api/v1/incidents`, `POST .../verify` |
| Actions | `GET /api/v1/corrective-actions`, evidence & verify |
| Risk | `GET /api/v1/risk/factors` |
| GIS | `GET /api/v1/gis/nodes`, `/gis/spatial-risk` |
| Officer | `GET /api/v1/officer/stats`, `POST .../inspections` |
| Notifications | `GET/PATCH /api/v1/notifications` |
| Auth | `POST /api/v1/auth/login` |

Responses use **camelCase** to match existing TypeScript types. In `DEBUG=true`, endpoints work without JWT so the current frontend role switcher keeps working; set `DEBUG=false` in production to require authentication.

# BioShield Backend — Analysis Report

Read-only analysis of `backend/`. No files were modified.

---

## 1. Backend Framework

**FastAPI** (Python), served with **Uvicorn**.

Supporting stack:
- **Pydantic v2** — request/response validation
- **SQLAlchemy 2** — ORM (currently bundled in this repo)
- **Alembic** — migrations (currently bundled)
- **python-jose** + **passlib** — JWT auth
- **PostgreSQL** via `psycopg2-binary`

---

## 2. Command to Run the Backend

From the `backend/` directory:

```powershell
uvicorn app.main:app --reload --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
```

Full startup (first time):

```powershell
cd backend
copy .env.example .env
python -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
alembic upgrade head
python -m scripts.seed
uvicorn app.main:app --reload --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
```

---

## 3. Main Entry File

**`backend/app/main.py`**

- Defines `create_app()` and exports `app` (the ASGI app Uvicorn loads).
- Mounts routers under `/api/v1`.
- Registers CORS, error handling, static uploads at `/uploads`.
- Exposes `GET /health`.

---

## 4–5. Every API Endpoint

Base prefix: **`/api/v1`**  
Responses use **camelCase** JSON (via Pydantic `serialize_by_alias=True`).

Auth: optional when `DEBUG=true`; required when `DEBUG=false` for role-protected routes.

---

| Static | `/uploads/{filename}` | Serve uploaded files | — | File binary |

## 6. Database-Related Code (Important for Your Team Split)

The repo currently includes a **full database layer**, not just API stubs. If another teammate owns the database, these areas overlap:

| Location | What it contains |
|----------|------------------|
| `app/database/base.py` | SQLAlchemy `Base` |
| `app/database/session.py` | Engine, `SessionLocal`, `get_db()` dependency |
| `app/models/` | 12 ORM entity files + enums (`User`, `Farm`, `Incident`, `CorrectiveAction`, `RiskFactor`, etc.) |
| `alembic/` | Migration config + `001_initial_schema.py` |
| `alembic.ini` | Alembic settings |
| `scripts/seed.py` | Demo data loader (4 farms, users, incidents, etc.) |
| `docker-compose.yml` | PostgreSQL 16 container |
| All `app/services/*.py` | Direct SQLAlchemy queries — no repository abstraction |
| All routers | Inject `db: Session = Depends(get_db)` |

**Every API endpoint depends on PostgreSQL being up and migrated.** There is no in-memory or mock fallback in the backend.

---

## 7. AI / Risk Engine Code (Important for Your Team Split)

There is **no external ML/AI service**. Risk logic is **rule-based Python** inside the API repo:

| Location | What it does |
|----------|--------------|
| `app/services/risk_service.py` — `RiskEngine` | Score = `100 - sum(active factor deltas)`; risk level thresholds; history; farm counter updates |
| `app/utils/helpers.py` | `farm_risk_level()` (70/40 thresholds), `incident_severity()` (by `numberAffected`), `haversine_km()` for GIS distance |
| `app/services/passport_service.py` | Hardcoded `ASSESSMENT_QUESTIONS` (Q001–Q005); weighted score → passport update |
| `app/services/incident_service.py` | On incident create: adds `RiskFactor`, calls `RiskEngine.recalculate_farm()`; on verify: auto-generates corrective actions |
| `app/services/corrective_action_service.py` | On evidence approval: compliance closure → passport update → risk recalculation |
| `app/services/officer_service.py` — `GisService` | Spatial proximity using haversine; containment zone lookup |
| `app/models/risk.py` | `RiskFactor`, `RiskScoreHistory` tables |

**Not present:**
- No ML model files
- No `RISK_ENGINE_URL` env var (mentioned in integration plan only)
- No calls to external AI APIs
- No WebSocket telemetry endpoint (frontend still uses client-side simulation)

If your AI/Risk team owns the engine, they would likely replace or externalize `RiskEngine`, assessment scoring, and spatial risk logic.

## 9. Can the Backend Run Independently?

**Partially.**

| Component | Independent? |
|-----------|--------------|
| FastAPI app import / `GET /health` | Yes — no DB needed |
| All `/api/v1/*` endpoints | **No** — requires PostgreSQL + migrations |
| File uploads | Yes — creates local `uploads/` directory |
| Frontend | Not required to run the API |

**Hard dependency:** running PostgreSQL with schema applied (`alembic upgrade head`).

**Soft dependency:** `python -m scripts.seed` for meaningful test data (empty DB returns empty lists / 404s).

## FRONTEND

src/

├── main.tsx

## BACKEND

### Framework

### Structure
```
backend/
├── app/
│   ├── main.py             # Entry point

| Live events timeline | `FarmerDashboard` | `useSimulation()` | **Not backend** (simulation) |

| Report incident | `IncidentReportForm` | `incidentService.submitIncident` | `POST /incidents/json` |
| Vet incident queue | `VetDashboard` | `incidentService` | `GET /incidents`, `POST .../verify` |
| Corrective actions | `CorrectiveActionsList` | `correctiveActionService` | `GET /corrective-actions`, verify |
| Evidence upload | `EvidenceUploadModal` | `correctiveActionService.submitEvidence` | `POST .../evidence/json` |
| Risk factors | `RiskDashboard` | `riskService.getRiskFactors()` | `GET /risk/factors` |
| Risk history chart | `RiskDashboard` | **Hardcoded in JSX** | `GET /risk/farms/{id}/history` exists but **not wired** |
| GIS map | `GisFarmMap` | `gisService` | `GET /gis/nodes` |
| Officer stats + farm table | `OfficerDashboard` | `officerService`, `farmService` | `GET /officer/stats`, `GET /farms` |
| Risk distribution bars | `OfficerDashboard` | **Hardcoded percentages** | Could derive from `/officer/stats` |
| Notifications | `NotificationCenter` | `notificationService` | `GET /notifications`, `PATCH .../read` |
| Simulation bar | `App.tsx` | `useSimulation()` | **Not backend** (presentation mode) |

| Schedule Inspection button | `OfficerDashboard` | **No handler** | `POST /officer/inspections` exists but **not wired** |

## Step 1 — Install PostgreSQL (required for backend)

Pick **one** option:

### Option A — Docker Desktop (recommended)
1. Install [Docker Desktop for Windows](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/)
2. Restart PC if asked
3. Then run:

```powershell
cd C:\Users\ullas\Downloads\FARM-PLATFORM--main\FARM-PLATFORM--main\backend
docker compose up -d
```

### Option B — PostgreSQL directly
1. Install from https://www.postgresql.org/download/windows/
2. During setup, set:
   - User: `bioshield`
   - Password: `bioshield`
   - Database: `bioshield`
   - Port: `5432`
3. Or ask your **database teammate** to give you a `DATABASE_URL` you can put in `backend\.env`

## Common problems

| Problem | Fix |
|---------|-----|
| `connection refused` on port 8000 | Start the backend (Terminal 1) |
| `could not connect to server` (PostgreSQL) | Install/start PostgreSQL (Step 1) |
| Farm dropdown shows only mock farm | Backend not running or DB not seeded — run `alembic upgrade head` + `python -m scripts.seed` |
| CORS error in browser | Ensure backend `CORS_ORIGINS` includes `http://localhost:5173` in `backend\.env` |
| Frontend shows empty data | Run `python -m scripts.seed` after migrations |

**Short answer:** Yes — **keep it for your SIH presentation**. It is **not** part of your backend scope, and you do **not** need it for a production system.

## What the simulation button does

The footer bar labeled **“Telemetry Simulator (SIH Presentation Mode)”** is a **client-side demo engine**. It:

- Fakes **live farm telemetry** (events, alerts, risk changes, Aarohi advisor messages)
- Runs on a timer with **Run / Pause / Reset** and **1× / 2× / 5×** speed
- Does **not** call your backend API — it lives in `src/simulation/`

Your backend handles real data: farms, incidents, passport, GIS, notifications, etc.

## Should you show it while presenting?

| Scenario | Recommendation |
|----------|----------------|
| **Full demo to judges** (show the portal “feels alive”) | **Yes — use it** |
| **Your part only** (backend/API integration) | **Optional** — backend works without it |
| **Final production product** | **No** — replace with real IoT telemetry / WebSocket from your hardware/AI teammates |

## What judges will see if you press Run

- **Farmer dashboard** — live event feed and Aarohi messages update (from simulation)
- **Farm name, score, incidents, map, vet queue** — still from your **real backend** (when it’s running)

## Practical presentation tip

1. Start backend + frontend (as you already have).
2. Show **real API flows** first: report incident → vet verifies → officer GIS view.
3. Switch to **Farmer** role and press **▶ Run** to show “live monitoring” without real sensors.

**Bottom line:** The simulation button is a **presentation helper**, not a backend requirement. For SIH demo day it’s useful; for your backend deliverable you can ignore it. Coordinate with your frontend teammate — they own that bar.

# Connecting Frontend + Backend After Render Deploy

Your setup is already wired for this — the frontend reads the backend URL from one env variable. You mainly need to deploy both sides and set the right environment variables.

---

## Architecture (how they connect)

```
User Browser
    ↓
Frontend (Vercel / Netlify / Render Static)
    ↓  fetch("https://YOUR-BACKEND.onrender.com/api/v1/...")
Backend (Render Web Service)
    ↓
PostgreSQL (Render Postgres or external)
```

The link is in `src/services/api.ts`:

```14:15:FARM-PLATFORM--main/src/services/api.ts
const API_BASE = import.meta.env.VITE_API_BASE_URL || "http://localhost:8000";
const API_V1 = `${API_BASE}/api/v1`;
```

---

## Step 1 — Deploy backend on Render

### A. Create PostgreSQL on Render
1. Render Dashboard → **New → PostgreSQL**
2. Copy the **Internal Database URL** (use this for the backend on Render)

### B. Create Web Service for backend
1. **New → Web Service** → connect your GitHub repo `BACKEND-FARM-`
2. Settings:

| Setting | Value |
|---------|--------|
| **Root Directory** | `backend` |
| **Runtime** | Python 3 |
| **Build Command** | `pip install -r requirements.txt` |
| **Start Command** | `uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT` |

### C. Environment variables on Render (backend)

```env
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://...   # from Render Postgres
JWT_SECRET=your-long-random-secret-here
JWT_ALGORITHM=HS256
DEBUG=false
APP_ENV=production
CORS_ORIGINS=https://YOUR-FRONTEND-DOMAIN.com,http://localhost:5173
STORAGE_BASE_URL=https://YOUR-BACKEND.onrender.com/uploads
```

Important:
- Set **`DEBUG=false`** in production (with `DEBUG=true`, auth is bypassed)
- **`CORS_ORIGINS`** must include your live frontend URL exactly (no trailing slash)
- Use a strong **`JWT_SECRET`**

### D. Run migrations + seed (once)

In Render → your service → **Shell**:

```bash
alembic upgrade head
python -m scripts.seed
```

Your backend URL will be something like:
`https://bioshield-api.onrender.com`

Verify:
- `https://YOUR-BACKEND.onrender.com/health` → `{"status":"ok"}`
- `https://YOUR-BACKEND.onrender.com/docs` → Swagger UI

---

## Step 2 — Deploy frontend

Deploy on **Vercel**, **Netlify**, or **Render Static Site**.

### Environment variable (frontend)

```env
VITE_API_BASE_URL=https://YOUR-BACKEND.onrender.com
```

No `/api/v1` at the end — the code adds that automatically.

Rebuild/redeploy the frontend after setting this (Vite bakes env vars at **build time**).

---

## Step 3 — Verify connection

1. Open your live frontend URL
2. Press **F12 → Network**
3. Refresh — you should see requests to `https://YOUR-BACKEND.onrender.com/api/v1/farms`
4. Farm dropdown should show real farms (GreenValley, SunRise, etc.)

If you see **CORS errors**:
- Add your frontend URL to backend `CORS_ORIGINS` on Render
- Redeploy backend

If farms don't load:
- Check backend `/health`
- Confirm Postgres is migrated and seeded
- Confirm `VITE_API_BASE_URL` is correct and frontend was rebuilt

---

## Quick reference diagram

```
┌─────────────────────┐     VITE_API_BASE_URL      ┌──────────────────────┐
│  Frontend           │ ─────────────────────────► │  Render Backend      │
│  (Vercel/Netlify)   │   https://xxx.onrender.com │  FastAPI :8000       │
│  yoursite.com       │                            │  /api/v1/*           │
└─────────────────────┘                            └──────────┬───────────┘
                                                              │
                                                              ▼
                                                   ┌──────────────────────┐
                                                   │  Render PostgreSQL   │
                                                   └──────────────────────┘
```

---

## Is your API good enough?

**Yes — for SIH demo and MVP integration.** It covers the main product flows.

### What you have (strong)

| Area | Status |
|------|--------|
| **Auth** | JWT login, register, refresh, `/me` |
| **Farms** | List, detail, passport, checklist, assessments |
| **Incidents** | Report, list, verify (vet workflow) |
| **Corrective actions** | List, evidence, verify |
| **Risk** | Factors, history, summary, recalculate |
| **GIS** | Map nodes, spatial risk |
| **Officer** | Stats, inspections, priority farms |
| **Notifications** | Role-based, mark read |
| **Health records** | CRUD + file upload |
| **Docs** | Swagger at `/docs` |
| **Health check** | `/health` for Render monitoring |
| **Frontend contract** | camelCase JSON matches TypeScript types |

That’s **40+ endpoints** — enough for a working portal demo.

### Gaps to know about (not blockers for demo)

| Gap | Impact | Who fixes |
|-----|--------|-----------|
| **`DEBUG=true` in prod** | Auth bypass | You — set `DEBUG=false` on Render |
| **File uploads on Render disk** | Files lost on redeploy | Use S3/Cloudinary later, or accept for demo |
| **No WebSocket / live IoT** | No real-time sensor stream | Hardware / AI teammate |
| **Risk engine is rule-based** | Not ML | AI teammate (optional upgrade) |
| **Frontend role switcher** | Not real login UI yet | Frontend teammate — `authService` already exists |
| **Some UI charts still static** | RiskDashboard history bars | Frontend can wire `GET /risk/farms/{id}/history` |
| **Render free tier cold start** | First request ~30–60s slow | Upgrade or warn judges before demo |

### Verdict for SIH presentation

| Question | Answer |
|----------|--------|
| API complete for demo? | **Yes** |
| API production-ready as-is? | **Almost** — set `DEBUG=false`, fix CORS, use managed Postgres |
| Good enough for your backend role? | **Yes** — solid FastAPI REST API with clear frontend integration |

---

## Production checklist before judges see it

```text
☐ DEBUG=false on Render
☐ Strong JWT_SECRET set
☐ CORS_ORIGINS includes live frontend URL
☐ PostgreSQL migrated + seeded
☐ VITE_API_BASE_URL points to Render backend
☐ Frontend rebuilt after env change
☐ Test /health and /api/v1/farms from browser
☐ Test incident report → vet verify flow live
```

# Render deploy — explained simply from Step 1

You’re deploying **two separate things** on Render:

1. **Database (PostgreSQL)** — stores farms, users, incidents  
2. **Backend (Python API)** — your code that reads/writes that data  

The frontend (website) talks to the **backend**, and the backend talks to the **database**.

---

## Step 1 — Create PostgreSQL (the database)

### What is this?

Your backend code **cannot save data by itself**. It needs a database — like an Excel file in the cloud that always stays online.

Locally you used **Docker** for PostgreSQL. On Render, you create Render’s own PostgreSQL instead.

### What to do

1. Go to [render.com](https://render.com) and log in  
2. Click the blue **New +** button (top right)  
3. Choose **PostgreSQL** (not Web Service yet)  
4. Fill in:
   - **Name:** `bioshield-db` (any name is fine)
   - **Region:** same as you’ll use for backend (e.g. Oregon)
   - **Plan:** Free (for demo)
5. Click **Create Database**  
6. Wait 1–2 minutes until it says **Available**

### What you need to copy

After it’s ready, open the database page. You’ll see two URLs:

| URL type | What it’s for |
|----------|----------------|
| **Internal Database URL** | Backend on Render → database (use this in Step 2) |
| **External Database URL** | Your laptop → database (use this only for seeding from your PC) |

They look like:
```
postgresql://bioshield_user:somepassword@dpg-xxxxx/bioshield
```

**Save both** somewhere (Notepad). You’ll need them later.

### Why do this first?

When you create the backend (Step 2), you must paste `DATABASE_URL` immediately. Without a database, the API starts but **crashes** when anything tries to load farms or incidents.

---

## Step 2 — Create the Web Service (your backend API)

### What is this?

This runs your **Python/FastAPI code** 24/7 on the internet so the frontend can call it.

### What to do

1. **New +** → **Web Service**  
2. Connect GitHub repo: `ullassallu28-eng/BACKEND-FARM-`  
3. Fill the form **exactly** like this:

| Field | Value |
|-------|--------|
| Name | `bioshield-api` |
| Language | **Python 3** |
| Branch | `main` |
| Root Directory | `backend` |
| Build Command | `pip install -r requirements.txt && alembic upgrade head` |
| Start Command | `uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT` |

**Root Directory = `backend`** means: “Ignore the React frontend; only deploy the Python folder.”

### What those commands mean

- **`pip install -r requirements.txt`** — install Python packages  
- **`alembic upgrade head`** — create tables in PostgreSQL  
- **`uvicorn app.main:app ...`** — start the API server  

### Environment variables (important)

Scroll to **Environment Variables** and add:

| Name | Value |
|------|--------|
| `DATABASE_URL` | Paste **Internal Database URL** from Step 1 |
| `JWT_SECRET` | Any long random text, e.g. `mySuperSecretKey2026BioShieldFarm` |
| `DEBUG` | `false` |
| `APP_ENV` | `production` |
| `CORS_ORIGINS` | `http://localhost:5173` |
| `STORAGE_BASE_URL` | `https://bioshield-api.onrender.com/uploads` *(use your service name)* |

Then click **Deploy Web Service**.

### How to know it worked

Wait for deploy to finish (green **Live**). Open in browser:

- `https://bioshield-api.onrender.com/health`  
  → should show: `{"status":"ok","service":"BioShield API"}`

- `https://bioshield-api.onrender.com/docs`  
  → Swagger API documentation page  

If `/health` works, **Step 2 is done**.

---

## Step 3 — Seed demo data (put sample farms in the database)

### What is this?

Migrations create **empty tables**. **Seed** fills them with demo farms, users, and incidents (same as `python -m scripts.seed` locally).

### Why from your PC?

Render **Free** plan has no Shell, so you run seed once from your laptop using the **External Database URL**.

### What to do

Open PowerShell:

```powershell
cd C:\Users\ullas\Downloads\FARM-PLATFORM--main\FARM-PLATFORM--main\backend
.venv\Scripts\activate
```

Set the **External** URL from Render Postgres (not Internal):

```powershell
$env:DATABASE_URL="postgresql://...."   # paste External URL here
python -m scripts.seed
```

You should see:
```
Seed completed successfully.
```

### How to verify

Open in browser:
```
https://bioshield-api.onrender.com/api/v1/farms
```

You should see JSON with farms like **GreenValley Bio-Farm**.

---

## Step 4 — Connect the frontend (your website)

### What is this?

Your React app must know **where the live API is**. Locally it used `http://localhost:8000`. In production it needs your Render URL.

### If frontend is still on your PC

Edit `.env` in project root:

```env
VITE_API_BASE_URL=https://bioshield-api.onrender.com
```

Restart frontend:

```powershell
npm run dev
```

### If frontend is deployed (Vercel / Netlify)

Add the same variable in their dashboard:

```
VITE_API_BASE_URL = https://bioshield-api.onrender.com
```

Then **redeploy** the frontend (env vars only apply at build time).

### Update CORS on backend

When you have a live frontend URL (e.g. `https://my-farm.vercel.app`), go to Render → backend → **Environment**:

```
CORS_ORIGINS=https://my-farm.vercel.app,http://localhost:5173
```

Save → Render redeploys automatically.

**CORS** = browser security. Backend must explicitly allow your frontend domain.

---

## Full picture

```
┌──────────────┐         ┌─────────────────────┐         ┌──────────────┐
│  Your PC or  │  HTTP   │  Render Web Service │  SQL    │ Render       │
│  Vercel      │ ──────► │  (Python API)       │ ──────► │ PostgreSQL   │
│  (Frontend)  │         │  bioshield-api      │         │ bioshield-db │
└──────────────┘         └─────────────────────┘         └──────────────┘
     Step 4                    Step 2                          Step 1
                               + seed (Step 3)
```

---

## Order to do things

```
1. Create PostgreSQL on Render          → get DATABASE_URL
2. Create Web Service (Python backend)  → paste DATABASE_URL, deploy
3. Seed from your PC                    → demo data in DB
4. Point frontend to Render URL         → website works live
```

---

## Common confusion

| Question | Answer |
|----------|--------|
| Do I deploy frontend on Render too? | Optional. Vercel is easier for React. Backend must be on Render (or similar). |
| Why Python 3, not Node? | API is in `backend/` (Python). Node is only for frontend. |
| Why two database URLs? | Internal = Render services talk to each other. External = your laptop connects. |
| Why is first request slow? | Free tier sleeps after inactivity; first hit wakes it (~30–60 sec). |
| What if `/farms` is empty `[]`? | You forgot Step 3 (seed). |

That’s normal — you still need one for the backend to work. Here’s what that means and what to do.

---

## Why you need a database

Your **backend code** (FastAPI) is only the logic. It does **not** store farms, users, or incidents by itself.

| Without database | With database |
|------------------|---------------|
| `/health` might work | Everything works |
| `/api/v1/farms` fails or is empty | Real farms, incidents, login data |
| Website shows mock/fallback data | Website shows real data |

Locally you used **Docker PostgreSQL**. On the internet you need a **cloud PostgreSQL** — the easiest option on Render is **Render PostgreSQL**.

Your DB teammate can own the schema later; for demo/deploy, **you create a Postgres instance on Render** and point the backend at it.

---

## What to do: create the database on Render (Step 1)

This **is** your database. You create it in about 2 minutes.

1. Go to [dashboard.render.com](https://dashboard.render.com)
2. Click **New +** → **PostgreSQL** (not Web Service)
3. Fill in:

| Field | Value |
|-------|--------|
| **Name** | `bioshield-db` |
| **Region** | Oregon (same as backend later) |
| **PostgreSQL Version** | 16 (default) |
| **Plan** | **Free** |

4. Click **Create Database**
5. Wait until status is **Available**

---

## Copy these two URLs

Open your new database → **Connections**:

| URL | Use for |
|-----|---------|
| **Internal Database URL** | Backend on Render → `DATABASE_URL` |
| **External Database URL** | Your PC → run seed once |

They look like:
```
postgresql://bioshield_user:abc123@dpg-xxxxx-a/bioshield_abc1
```

Save both in Notepad.

---

## Then connect backend to this database

When you create the **Web Service** (Python backend), add:

```env
DATABASE_URL=<paste Internal Database URL here>
```

The **Build Command** creates the tables:

```
pip install -r requirements.txt && alembic upgrade head
```

That replaces what `alembic upgrade head` did locally.

---

## Then add demo data (seed)

Tables start **empty**. Run once from your PC:

```powershell
cd C:\Users\ullas\Downloads\FARM-PLATFORM--main\FARM-PLATFORM--main\backend
.venv\Scripts\activate
$env:DATABASE_URL="postgresql://..."   # External Database URL from Render
python -m scripts.seed
```

After that, farms and users exist in the cloud database.

---

## Full order (you’re here)

```
① Create PostgreSQL on Render     ← YOU ARE HERE (no DB yet)
② Deploy Python backend on Render  → uses DATABASE_URL from ①
③ Seed from your PC                → fills DB with demo data
④ Vercel env VITE_API_BASE_URL     → frontend talks to backend
```

---

## About your DB teammate

| Situation | What to do |
|-----------|------------|
| Teammate hasn’t deployed DB yet | **You create Render Postgres** for demo — totally fine for SIH |
| Teammate gives you a URL later | Change `DATABASE_URL` on Render to theirs |
| Teammate owns schema/migrations | Your repo already has Alembic; they can take over later |

For the hackathon demo, **Render PostgreSQL + your backend + Vercel frontend** is enough.

---

## Quick check after all steps

Open in browser:

```
https://YOUR-BACKEND.onrender.com/api/v1/farms
```

- `[]` empty → seed not run yet (Step ③)  
- JSON with farms → database is working  

---

**Summary:** You don’t have a database **yet** — create **New → PostgreSQL** on Render. That becomes your project database. Without it, the backend cannot serve real data to your Vercel site.

## Things that can break deploy (fix on Render/Vercel)

### Render backend
1. **Wrong language** — must be **Python 3**, not Node  
2. **Missing Root Directory** — must be `backend`  
3. **No PostgreSQL** — create Render Postgres and set `DATABASE_URL`  
4. **Wrong start command** — use `uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT`  
5. **`DEBUG=true` in production** — set `DEBUG=false`  
6. **Missing CORS** — add your Vercel URL to `CORS_ORIGINS`  
7. **No seed** — run `python -m scripts.seed` once or `/farms` stays empty  

### Vercel frontend
1. **Missing `VITE_API_BASE_URL`** — set to your Render backend URL  
2. **No redeploy after env change** — must redeploy Vercel after adding the variable

## Why it's safe

| Concern | Answer |
|---------|--------|
| Will Render break? | **No** — Render only runs what's in `backend/` (Python). A markdown file in the repo root is ignored at runtime. |
| Will Vercel break? | **No** — Vercel builds from `package.json` / `npm run build`. It doesn't read random `.md` files. |
| Will the API stop working? | **No** — it's documentation only, not code. |
| Will it expose secrets? | **No** — the guide uses placeholders like `YOUR-VERCEL-APP.vercel.app`, not real passwords. |
| Will it increase build time? | **Negligible** — one small text file. |

## What it actually does

`DEPLOYMENT_GUIDE.md` is a **readme-style checklist** for you and your team. It helps with:

- Render PostgreSQL setup  
- Backend deploy settings  
- Vercel env vars  
- Seeding the database  

It does **not** get executed, imported, or deployed as part of the app.

BACKEND-FARM-/
├── DEPLOYMENT_GUIDE.md   ← docs only, harmless
├── backend/              ← Render deploys THIS

└── package.json
```

**Bottom line:** Pushing `DEPLOYMENT_GUIDE.md` is good practice — it documents how to deploy. It won't break Render, Vercel, or your project. You're fine.

# What to do on Render — step by step

You need **2 things** on Render: a **database** and a **backend API**.

---

## STEP 1 — Create PostgreSQL (database)

1. Go to https://dashboard.render.com
2. Click **New +** → **PostgreSQL**
3. Fill in:

| Field | Value |
|-------|--------|
| Name | `agrisentinel-db` |
| Region | **Oregon (US West)** |
| Plan | **Free** (for demo) |

4. Click **Create Database**
5. Wait until status = **Available**
6. Copy these from the **Connections** tab:
   - **Internal Database URL** → for backend
   - **External Database URL** → for seeding from your PC

---

## STEP 2 — Create Web Service (backend API)

1. **New +** → **Web Service**
2. Connect GitHub repo: `ullassallu28-eng/BACKEND-FARM-`
3. Fill in **exactly**:

| Field | Value |
|-------|--------|
| Name | `agrisentinel-api` |
| Language | **Python 3** (not Node) |
| Branch | `main` |
| Root Directory | `backend` |
| Build Command | `pip install -r requirements.txt && alembic upgrade head` |
| Start Command | `uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT` |
| Plan | Free (demo) or Starter (always on) |

---

## STEP 3 — Add environment variables

In the backend service → **Environment** → add:

```env
DATABASE_URL=<paste Internal Database URL from Step 1>

JWT_SECRET=your-long-random-secret-min-32-chars

JWT_ALGORITHM=HS256
DEBUG=false
APP_ENV=production
APP_NAME=AgriSentinel API

CORS_ORIGINS=https://YOUR-VERCEL-URL.vercel.app,http://localhost:5173

STORAGE_BASE_URL=https://agrisentinel-api.onrender.com/uploads
UPLOAD_DIR=uploads
DEFAULT_DISTRICT_ID=district-ranchi
```

Replace:
- `DATABASE_URL` → your Internal Postgres URL
- `YOUR-VERCEL-URL.vercel.app` → your real Vercel frontend URL
- `agrisentinel-api` → your actual Render service name if different

4. Click **Deploy**

---

## STEP 4 — Check backend is live

After deploy (green **Live**), open:

| URL | Expected |
|-----|----------|
| `https://agrisentinel-api.onrender.com/health` | `{"status":"ok","service":"AgriSentinel API"}` |
| `https://agrisentinel-api.onrender.com/docs` | Swagger API docs |
| `https://agrisentinel-api.onrender.com/api/v1/farms` | `[]` until seeded |

---

## STEP 5 — Seed demo data (from your PC)

Render Free has no Shell. Run once on your laptop:

```powershell
cd C:\Users\ullas\Downloads\FARM-PLATFORM--main\FARM-PLATFORM--main\backend
.venv\Scripts\activate

$env:DATABASE_URL="postgresql://..."   # External Database URL from Render

python -m scripts.seed
```

Then check: `https://agrisentinel-api.onrender.com/api/v1/farms` → should show 4 farms.

---

## STEP 6 — Connect Vercel frontend

1. Vercel → your project → **Settings** → **Environment Variables**
2. Add:

```env
VITE_API_BASE_URL=https://agrisentinel-api.onrender.com
```

3. **Redeploy** Vercel (required after env change)

---

## Visual summary

```
Render Dashboard
├── PostgreSQL (agrisentinel-db)     ← Step 1
└── Web Service (agrisentinel-api)   ← Step 2 + 3
         ↓
    Seed from PC                      ← Step 5
         ↓
    Vercel env + redeploy             ← Step 6
         ↓
    Live demo ready ✅
```

---

## Common mistakes on Render

| Mistake | Fix |
|---------|-----|
| Language = Node | Change to **Python 3** |
| No Root Directory | Set to **`backend`** |
| Wrong start command | Use `uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT` |
| CORS error on Vercel | Add exact Vercel URL to `CORS_ORIGINS` |
| Empty farms | Run seed (Step 5) |
| First request slow | Free tier cold start — wait 30–60 sec |

---

## Order to do things

```
1. PostgreSQL on Render
2. Web Service on Render (Python, backend/)
3. Add env vars → Deploy
4. Seed from your PC
5. Vercel VITE_API_BASE_URL → redeploy
6. Test live site
```

# Where real data comes from in AgriSentinel

There are **3 layers** — it helps to know which is which.

---

## 1. Demo / seed data (what you have now)

**Source:** `backend/scripts/seed.py`  
**Stored in:** PostgreSQL (local Docker or Render Postgres)

When you run:
```powershell
python -m scripts.seed
```

It inserts **sample data** into the database:

| Data | Examples |
|------|----------|
| Farms | GreenValley Bio-Farm, SunRise Poultry Haven |
| Users | farmer@bioshield.local, vet, officer |
| Incidents | Pre-loaded demo incidents |
| Checklist | Daily biosecurity tasks |
| Risk factors | Score contributors |
| GIS nodes | Farm map markers |
| Notifications | Bell icon alerts |

This is **real in the sense** that it lives in PostgreSQL and the API serves it — but it was **written by your team for demo**, not from live farms or sensors.

```
seed.py  →  PostgreSQL  →  FastAPI  →  Vercel frontend
```

---

## 2. User-generated data (real during demo)

**Source:** People using the website

When someone uses the live app, **new real records** are created in the database:

| Action | Data created |
|--------|----------------|
| **Report Incident** | New row in `incidents` table |
| **Vet verifies incident** | Updated status + notes |
| **Checklist tick** | Updated checklist item |
| **Submit evidence** | Corrective action evidence |
| **Officer schedules inspection** | New inspection record |

Example flow:
```
Farmer reports disease on website
    → POST /api/v1/incidents
    → Saved in PostgreSQL
    → Vet sees it in queue (real, just created)
```

So during your SIH demo, **anything you submit live is real data** — not fake animation.

---

## 3. Live farm / IoT data (future — teammate scope)

**Source:** Sensors, farm devices, government systems (not built yet)

| Data type | Who provides | Status |
|-----------|--------------|--------|
| Temperature, humidity sensors | Hardware / IoT teammate | Not connected |
| Live visitor/vehicle logs | Farm entry systems | Not connected |
| ML risk predictions | AI teammate | Rule-based engine only now |
| Govt registry farms | External API | Not connected |

That would look like:
```
Farm sensors  →  IoT gateway  →  Backend API  →  Dashboard
```

Your backend has placeholders for this (risk recalculate, health records) but **no live sensor feed yet**.

---

## Full picture

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    WHERE DATA COMES FROM                 │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                          │
│  ① SEED (one-time demo setup)                           │
│     seed.py → farms, users, sample incidents            │
│                                                          │
│  ② USER ACTIONS (live during demo) ✅ REAL             │
│     Report incident, verify, checklist, notifications │
│                                                          │
│  ③ SENSORS / ML / GOVT APIs (future)                    │
│     IoT teammate, AI teammate, DB teammate              │
│                                                          │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                          ↓
                   PostgreSQL Database
                          ↓
                   FastAPI Backend (Render)
                          ↓
                   React Frontend (Vercel)
```

---

# How to make AgriSentinel a **real** SIH 2026 solution (not just a demo)

Your problem statement (**SIH260487**) is:

> **Digital Farm Management Portal for Biosecurity Measures in Pig and Poultry Farms**

A **real solution** for judges means: real workflow, real database, live deployment, and a clear path to real farm data — not fake buttons or only seed data.

---

## What you have now vs what “real” means

| Level | What it is | Your status |
|-------|------------|-------------|
| **Demo** | Fake UI, mock data, localhost only | ❌ You moved past this |
| **Working prototype** | Real API + DB + deployed site + workflows | ✅ **You are here** |
| **Real solution** | Live farms/users + sensors/ML + govt-ready data | 🟡 **Next steps below** |

For SIH 2026, judges usually expect at least a **strong working prototype** with a **clear plan** for real-world rollout. You don’t need 1000 real farms on day one.

---

## What “real data” means for YOUR problem statement

The problem asks for a portal that handles **biosecurity for pig & poultry farms**. Real data comes from these sources:

### 1. Farm registration data (real farms)
**What:** Farm name, location, owner, capacity, animal type, GPS  
**How to get it:**
- Partner with 2–3 **local poultry/pig farms** in Jharkhand (Ranchi area matches your demo)
- Collect via a **registration form** on your portal (`POST /api/v1/farms` — already built)
- Or import from **Animal Husbandry Department** records (officer teammate / mentor help)

```
Real farmer registers on AgriSentinel
    → Saved in PostgreSQL
    → Shows on officer GIS map
```

### 2. Incident & disease reporting (real events)
**What:** Disease symptoms, affected animals, photos, location  
**How to get it:**
- Farmers/vets **report through your live website** (already works)
- Each report → real row in database → vet queue

**For SIH demo:** Report 1 incident live during presentation — that **is** real data.

### 3. Biosecurity checklist & compliance (real logs)
**What:** Daily disinfection, vaccination, visitor logs  
**How to get it:**
- Farmer ticks checklist daily on portal (`/farms/{id}/checklist` — already built)
- Officer sees compliance % on dashboard

**For real rollout:** Train 1–2 pilot farms to use checklist for 1 week → real compliance history.

### 4. Risk scoring (semi-real now, ML later)
**What:** Biosecurity score 0–100 based on incidents, mortality, sanitation  
**Now:** Rule-based engine in your backend (works with real inputs)  
**Real ML later:** AI teammate replaces rules with trained model on historical outbreak data

### 5. GIS / regional monitoring (real coordinates)
**What:** Farm locations on map, nearby outbreak zones  
**How to get it:**
- Use **real GPS** when registering farms (latitude/longitude fields exist)
- Officer dashboard + GIS map already consume `/api/v1/gis/nodes`

### 6. IoT / telemetry (future — hardware teammate)
**What:** Temperature, humidity, visitor counters, vehicle entry sensors  
**Not required for SIH demo**, but mention as Phase 2:
```
Sensors → MQTT/WebSocket → Backend → Live dashboard
```

---

# When your teammate gets real-time data — then what?

If a teammate brings **real-time data** (sensors, IoT, live farm feeds) for **SIH260487** (biosecurity for pig & poultry farms), it plugs into **AgriSentinel** like this:

---

## The big picture

```
Real-time source (teammate)          Your backend (you)              Frontend (Vercel)
─────────────────────────           ──────────────────              ─────────────────
Sensors / IoT / API          →      Receive & store          →      Live dashboard
MQTT / CSV / Python script          PostgreSQL + FastAPI            Farmer / Officer UI
```

**Their job:** collect and send data  
**Your job:** receive, save, expose via API  
**Frontend job:** show it live on the dashboard  

---

## Step 1 — Teammate defines the data format

Ask them to share a **sample JSON** for each reading, for example:

```json
{
  "farmId": "FARM-JH-2026-0487",
  "zoneId": "zone-shed-02",
  "type": "temperature",
  "value": 32.5,
  "unit": "celsius",
  "timestamp": "2026-08-11T14:30:00Z"
}
```

Or visitor/vehicle logs:

```json
{
  "farmId": "FARM-JH-2026-0487",
  "eventType": "visitor_entry",
  "name": "Dr. Sharma",
  "handHygieneCompleted": true,
  "timestamp": "2026-08-11T14:30:00Z"
}
```

**Agree on one format** so your backend can accept it.

---

## Step 2 — Teammate sends data to YOUR backend

They can use any of these (pick one):

| Method | Best for | Your backend adds |
|--------|----------|-------------------|
| **REST POST** | Simple, SIH demo | `POST /api/v1/telemetry/events` |
| **WebSocket** | True live stream | `WebSocket /ws/farms/{id}/telemetry` |
| **MQTT → your API** | IoT devices | Small bridge script → POST to your API |
| **Batch CSV import** | Historical data | `POST /api/v1/telemetry/import` |

**For SIH demo, REST POST is enough** — teammate sends data every few seconds with a script.

Example teammate script:

```python
import requests, time, random

while True:
    requests.post(
        "https://agrisentinel-api.onrender.com/api/v1/telemetry/events",
        json={
            "farmId": "FARM-JH-2026-0487",
            "type": "temperature",
            "value": round(random.uniform(28, 35), 1),
            "zoneId": "zone-shed-02"
        }
    )
    time.sleep(5)
```

---

## Step 3 — YOU store it in PostgreSQL

Your backend (or DB teammate) adds a table, e.g.:

```
farm_events / telemetry_readings
├── farm_id
├── zone_id
├── event_type
├── value / payload (JSON)
└── recorded_at
```

Flow:

```
Teammate POST → FastAPI router → Service → PostgreSQL
```

This matches what your integration plan already describes for `farm_events` / telemetry.

---

## Step 4 — Frontend reads live data

Today the farmer dashboard shows:
- **Incidents** from `/api/v1/incidents`
- **Checklist** from `/api/v1/farms/{id}/checklist`
- **Risk factors** from `/api/v1/risk/factors`

When telemetry exists, add either:

| Approach | How |
|----------|-----|
| **Polling** (easier) | Frontend calls `GET /api/v1/farms/{id}/telemetry` every 5–10 sec |
| **WebSocket** (better) | Frontend subscribes to live push |

**“Recent Farm Log Events”** on the farmer dashboard would then show **real sensor events**, not only incidents.

---

## Step 5 — Risk score updates automatically (AI teammate)

When real data arrives:

```
New telemetry (high temp / visitor without PPE)
    → AI / risk engine recalculates score
    → POST /api/v1/risk/farms/{id}/recalculate  (already exists)
    → Farm biosecurity score updates
    → Officer GIS map shows new risk level
```

Your backend already has `RiskEngine.recalculate_farm()` — wire it to run when telemetry crosses thresholds.

---

## What each person does

| Teammate | Delivers | Connects to |
|----------|----------|-------------|
| **IoT / data** | Sensor readings, visitor logs, scripts | Your `POST /telemetry` endpoint |
| **You (backend)** | API endpoint + DB table + store data | PostgreSQL + existing farms API |
| **DB teammate** | Table schema, indexes | `telemetry_readings` migration |
| **AI teammate** | Risk rules / ML on live data | `/risk/recalculate` |
| **Frontend** | Poll or WebSocket on dashboard | `api.ts` + FarmerDashboard events list |

---

## What you need to build (backend) — short list

When teammate has data ready:

1. **New model** — `TelemetryEvent` or `FarmEvent` in `backend/app/models/`
2. **New router** — `POST /api/v1/telemetry/events` (ingest)
3. **New router** — `GET /api/v1/farms/{id}/telemetry` (read latest)
4. **Alembic migration** — new table
5. **Optional** — trigger risk recalculate on critical events
6. **Share API URL + JSON format** with IoT teammate

Frontend change (minimal):

- FarmerDashboard “Recent Farm Log Events” → fetch from telemetry API instead of/in addition to incidents

---

## For SIH judges — what to say

> “Our IoT module streams real-time farm telemetry — temperature, visitor logs, sanitation events — into the AgriSentinel API. Data is stored in PostgreSQL and updates biosecurity risk scores and the regional GIS map in near real time.”

---

## Order of work

```
1. Teammate gets sensor/data source working
2. Agree JSON format (farmId, type, value, timestamp)
3. You add POST endpoint + DB table on Render
4. Teammate points script/devices at your live API URL
5. Frontend polls GET endpoint → live dashboard
6. AI teammate hooks risk recalculation
7. Demo: show number changing live on screen
```

---

## Important

| Question | Answer |
|----------|--------|
| Do you need this before Render deploy? | **No** — deploy backend + DB first |
| Can demo work without IoT? | **Yes** — incidents + checklist are already “real” |
| When teammate has data? | Add **one POST endpoint** — rest of app stays the same |
| Is simulation needed? | **No** — you removed it; real telemetry replaces it |

---

**Bottom line:** When your teammate has real-time data, they **send it to your backend API** → you **save in PostgreSQL** → **frontend shows it**. You are the **middle layer** between sensors and the portal. Deploy Render first; add a telemetry POST endpoint when their data is ready.

If you want, when they share their data format (JSON/CSV/MQTT), I can sketch the exact FastAPI endpoint and table for your repo.

# Deploy backend + DB first — what that means

**In plain words:** Put your **database** and **API** on the internet so your **Vercel website** can use them — not only your laptop.

Right now:
- Frontend → on **Vercel** (online)
- Backend + database → on **your PC** (offline for others)

After deploy:
- Frontend (Vercel) → Backend (Render) → Database (Render) — **all online 24/7**

---

## Part 1 — Deploy DB (database)

**What:** Create PostgreSQL on Render (cloud storage for farms, users, incidents).

**Steps:**
1. https://dashboard.render.com → **New +** → **PostgreSQL**
2. Name: `agrisentinel-db` → **Create**
3. Wait until **Available**
4. Copy **Internal Database URL** (save in Notepad)

**Result:** Empty database in the cloud, waiting for tables and data.

---

## Part 2 — Deploy backend (API)

**What:** Run your FastAPI code on Render so the world can call `https://your-api.onrender.com/api/v1/...`

**Steps:**
1. **New +** → **Web Service** → repo `BACKEND-FARM-`
2. Settings:

| Field | Value |
|-------|--------|
| Language | **Python 3** |
| Root Directory | `backend` |
| Build Command | `pip install -r requirements.txt && alembic upgrade head` |
| Start Command | `uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT` |

3. **Environment variables:**

```env
DATABASE_URL=<Internal Database URL from Part 1>
JWT_SECRET=any-long-random-secret-32-chars
DEBUG=false
APP_ENV=production
APP_NAME=AgriSentinel API
CORS_ORIGINS=https://YOUR-VERCEL-URL.vercel.app,http://localhost:5173
STORAGE_BASE_URL=https://YOUR-SERVICE-NAME.onrender.com/uploads
```

4. **Deploy** → wait for green **Live**

**Result:** API online. Tables created by `alembic upgrade head` during build.

---

## Part 3 — Put demo data in cloud DB (seed)

**What:** Fill the online database with farms/users (same as `seed.py` locally).

**On your PC:**
```powershell
cd backend
.venv\Scripts\activate
$env:DATABASE_URL="<External Database URL from Render Postgres>"
python -m scripts.seed
```

**Result:** Live API returns real farms at `/api/v1/farms`.

---

## Part 4 — Connect Vercel

**What:** Tell frontend where the live API is.

1. Vercel → Project → **Settings** → **Environment Variables**
2. Add: `VITE_API_BASE_URL=https://YOUR-SERVICE-NAME.onrender.com`
3. **Redeploy** Vercel

**Result:** Your website uses cloud API, not `localhost:8000`.

---

## How to know it worked

| Check | URL |
|-------|-----|
| API alive | `https://YOUR-API.onrender.com/health` |
| Has farms | `https://YOUR-API.onrender.com/api/v1/farms` |
| Website works | Your Vercel URL → farm dropdown shows farms |

---

## One-line summary

```
Deploy DB first  →  Deploy backend second  →  Seed data  →  Connect Vercel
   (PostgreSQL)        (FastAPI on Render)      (seed.py)     (env var)
```

---

## Why “first”?

| If you skip deploy | Problem |
|--------------------|---------|
| IoT teammate sends data | Nowhere to send it (no public API URL) |
| Judges open Vercel site | No farms / errors (no live backend) |
| Team tests from phones | localhost doesn’t work |

Deploy backend + DB **first** → then IoT, ML, and demo all have a **live URL** to connect to.

---

# You don’t need data or a database before Part 1

**Part 1 is where you CREATE the database.** You are not expected to already have one.

---

## What you might be thinking

| Wrong idea | Reality |
|------------|---------|
| “We need data first, then create DB” | **No** — create empty DB first, add data later |
| “Our DB teammate must finish first” | **No** — you can create Render Postgres yourself for SIH |
| “We have no database at all” | **Correct** — Part 1 **gives** you one |

---

## What Part 1 actually does

```
Before Part 1:
  ❌ No cloud database
  ❌ No place for farms/users online

After Part 1 (click Create PostgreSQL on Render):
  ✅ Empty database exists in the cloud
  ✅ You get a URL (DATABASE_URL)
  ✅ Ready for backend to connect
```

**Empty is normal.** Every new database starts empty.

---

## Where data comes later (not Part 1)

```
Part 1  →  Create EMPTY database on Render
Part 2  →  Backend connects + creates TABLES (alembic)
Part 3  →  seed.py fills DEMO data (farms, users)
Later   →  Users report incidents = NEW real data
Later   →  IoT teammate sends sensor data
```

---

## Simple analogy

| Step | Like… |
|------|--------|
| Part 1 (Render Postgres) | **Building an empty warehouse** |
| Part 2 (backend + alembic) | **Adding shelves (tables)** |
| Part 3 (seed) | **Putting sample boxes in** |
| Live use | **Farmers add new boxes daily** |

You don’t need boxes before building the warehouse.

---

## What to do right now (Part 1 only)

1. Go to https://dashboard.render.com

# What your **database friend** does vs what **you** do

When **real data** comes in, both of you work together — but different parts.

---

## Simple split

| Person | Main job |
|--------|----------|
| **You (backend)** | API — receive data, business logic, connect frontend |
| **DB friend (database)** | Database — design tables, store data safely, migrations, queries |

```
Real data (IoT / farms / govt)
        ↓
   YOUR API (backend)     ← you build endpoints
        ↓
   PostgreSQL            ← DB friend owns structure & data quality
        ↓
   Frontend (Vercel)
```

---

## What your DB friend does (real data)

### 1. Design the database schema
- Tables for farms, incidents, telemetry, users, etc.
- Relationships (farm → zones → events)
- Data types, constraints, indexes

**Example:** When IoT sends temperature readings, they define:

```
telemetry_readings
├── id
├── farm_id
├── sensor_id
├── temperature
├── recorded_at
```

You already have Alembic migrations in `backend/alembic/` — your friend can **own and extend** those.

---

### 2. Write / review migrations
- `alembic revision` for new tables (telemetry, sensors, etc.)
- Run `alembic upgrade head` on Render/production
- Keep schema in sync with the problem statement

**They change:** SQL tables  
**You change:** Python models + API routes to match

---

### 3. Import real farm data
- Real farm names, locations, owners from Jharkhand / govt / pilot partners
- Bulk import (CSV → SQL or seed script)
- Replace or add to demo seed data

**Example:**
```sql
INSERT INTO farms (id, name, location, latitude, longitude, ...)
VALUES ('FARM-REAL-001', 'Actual Poultry Farm Ranchi', ...);
```

---

### 4. Data quality & security
- Valid data only (no junk from sensors)
- Backups on Render Postgres
- Who can read/write what (farmer sees own farm, officer sees district)
- Indexes so queries stay fast with lots of telemetry

---

### 5. Queries for reports (optional)
- Officer stats: farms by risk level per district
- Compliance reports for judges / govt
- Help you with complex SQL if needed

---

## What **you** do (backend) — not DB friend

| Task | Owner |
|------|--------|
| `POST /api/v1/incidents` | **You** |
| `POST /api/v1/telemetry/events` (when IoT ready) | **You** |
| JWT auth, CORS, Render deploy | **You** |
| Risk recalculation logic | **You** (+ AI teammate) |
| Table design & migrations | **DB friend** |
| Import real farm list CSV | **DB friend** (or together) |
| Production backup strategy | **DB friend** |

---

## When real-time data arrives (IoT teammate)

| Step | Who |
|------|-----|
| Sensor sends JSON | IoT teammate |
| `POST /telemetry` endpoint | **You** |
| `telemetry_readings` table | **DB friend** creates migration |
| Store row in PostgreSQL | **You** (code uses their table) |
| Show on dashboard | Frontend teammate |

**Flow:**
```
IoT → Your API → DB friend's table → Frontend
```

---

## For SIH demo — who does what now

| Task | Who | When |
|------|-----|------|
| Create Render Postgres | **You** (now) | Demo |
| Run migrations | **You** (build command) | Demo |
| Run seed.py (demo farms) | **You** | Demo |
| Real farm import | **DB friend** | Before final demo |
| Telemetry tables | **DB friend** | When IoT has data |
| Live API on Render | **You** | Now |

**For hackathon:** You can deploy with **seed data**; DB friend adds **real farms** later by import or updated seed.

You're on the right page. It says **No Environment Variables Added** — add one now.

---

## Steps

### 1. Click **Add Environment Variable** (or **Add New**)

Usually a button at the top right of that section.

---

### 2. Fill the form

| Field | What to type |
|-------|----------------|
| **Key** (Name) | `VITE_API_BASE_URL` |
| **Value** | `https://agrisentinel-api.onrender.com` |

**Important:** No slash at the end. No `/api/v1`.

---

### 3. Select environments

Check all three:

- ✅ **Production**
- ✅ **Preview**
- ✅ **Development**

---

### 4. Click **Save**

---

### 5. Redeploy (required)

1. Go to **Deployments** (top menu)
2. Find the latest deployment
3. Click **⋯** (three dots) on the right
4. Click **Redeploy**
5. Wait until status is **Ready**

Env vars only apply after a new deploy.

Save.

# Why BioShield still shows

Your **GitHub repo** already has **AgriSentinel** (no simulator).  
Vercel is still serving an **old build** or a **different repo**.

---

## Fix — check Vercel Git connection

### Step 1 — See which repo Vercel uses

1. Vercel → your project (**farm-platform-gilt**)
2. **Settings** → **Git**
3. Check **Connected Git Repository**

**Should be:**
```
ullassallu28-eng/BACKEND-FARM-
```

**If it shows a different repo** (e.g. `FARM-PLATFORM` or another name) → that’s why you still see BioShield.

---

## Option A — Vercel is NOT connected to BACKEND-FARM-

1. **Settings** → **Git** → **Disconnect** (if needed)
2. **Add Git Repository** → select **`ullassallu28-eng/BACKEND-FARM-`**
3. Settings:

| Setting | Value |
|---------|--------|
| **Root Directory** | leave **empty** (repo root) |
| **Framework** | Vite |
| **Build Command** | `npm run build` |
| **Output Directory** | `dist` |

4. **Environment Variable** (add again):

```
VITE_API_BASE_URL=https://agrisentinel-api.onrender.com
```

5. **Deploy**

---

## Option B — Vercel IS connected to BACKEND-FARM-

Force a fresh deploy:

1. **Deployments** tab
2. Latest deployment → **⋯** → **Redeploy**
3. Check **Use existing Build Cache** → **OFF** / unchecked
4. Redeploy

Or push a tiny change to trigger deploy:

```powershell
cd C:\Users\ullas\Downloads\FARM-PLATFORM--main\FARM-PLATFORM--main
git commit --allow-empty -m "Trigger Vercel redeploy for AgriSentinel branding."
git push origin main
```

### Part 3 — Connect the correct repo

## Update CORS on Render — step by step

### Step 1 — Open Render
1. Go to **https://dashboard.render.com**
2. Log in

---

### Step 2 — Open your API service
1. On the dashboard, click **`agrisentinel-api`**
   - (Web Service — not the database)

---

### Step 3 — Open Environment settings
1. In the left sidebar, click **Environment**
2. You’ll see a list of variables like `DATABASE_URL`, `JWT_SECRET`, `CORS_ORIGINS`, etc.

---

### Step 4 — Edit `CORS_ORIGINS`

1. Find **`CORS_ORIGINS`**
2. Click **Edit** (pencil icon) or change the value
3. Set it to your **new Vercel URL**:

```
https://backend-farm.vercel.app,http://localhost:5173
```

**Replace** `backend-farm.vercel.app` with your **actual** Vercel URL from the new project.

Examples:
```
https://backend-farm-abc123.vercel.app,http://localhost:5173
```

Or if you use both old and new URLs temporarily:
```
https://backend-farm.vercel.app,https://farm-platform-gilt.vercel.app,http://localhost:5173
```

4. **No spaces** after commas
5. **No trailing slash** on URLs

---

### Step 5 — Save
1. Click **Save Changes**
2. Render will **automatically redeploy** the API (~1–2 min)
3. Wait until status shows **Live** again

---

### Step 6 — Test
1. Open your new Vercel site
2. Hard refresh: **`Ctrl + Shift + R`**
3. Farm dropdown should load **4 farms**

---

The vet queue stuck on **“Loading incoming incidents…”** usually means the frontend **can’t reach the API**. The API itself has incidents (I confirmed that).

---

## Most likely cause

**`VITE_API_BASE_URL` was not set** when you deployed **`backend-farm`** on Vercel.

Without it, the site calls `http://localhost:8000` instead of Render.

---

## Fix — step by step

### Step 1 — Add env variable on Vercel

1. Vercel → project **`backend-farm`**
2. **Settings** → **Environment Variables**
3. Add (or update):

   | Key | Value |
   |-----|--------|
   | `VITE_API_BASE_URL` | `https://agrisentinel-api.onrender.com` |

4. Enable for **Production**, **Preview**, and **Development**
5. **Save**

---

### Step 2 — Redeploy (required)

Env vars only apply after a new build:

1. **Deployments** → **⋯** → **Redeploy**
2. **Clear build cache** → **ON**
3. **Redeploy**
4. Wait until **Ready**

---

### Step 3 — Confirm CORS URL matches exactly

1. Vercel → **backend-farm** → copy your **exact** domain  
   (e.g. `backend-farm.vercel.app` or `backend-farm-xxxxx.vercel.app`)
2. Render → **agrisentinel-api** → **Environment** → `CORS_ORIGINS`:

   ```
   https://YOUR-EXACT-VERCEL-URL,http://localhost:5173
   ```

3. **Save Changes** → wait until **Live**

---

### Step 4 — Test again

1. Open **https://backend-farm.vercel.app**
2. Hard refresh: **`Ctrl + Shift + R`**
3. First load may take **30–60 seconds** (Render cold start)
4. Switch to **Veterinarian** → you should see incidents in the queue

---

1. **Farmer** → **Report Incident** → Submit  
2. Then **Veterinarian** → refresh → new incident should appear

## Main fix — set API URL on Vercel

Your frontend was likely built **without** the API URL, so it tries `localhost:8000` instead of Render.

### Do this on Vercel (`backend-farm` project):

1. **Settings** → **Environment Variables**
2. Add or update:

   | Key | Value |
   |-----|--------|
   | `VITE_API_BASE_URL` | `https://agrisentinel-api.onrender.com` |

3. Enable for **Production**, **Preview**, **Development**
4. **Save**
5. **Deployments** → **Redeploy** → **Clear build cache ON** → **Redeploy**
6. Wait until **Ready** (~2 min)

---

## Then test submit

1. Open **https://backend-farm.vercel.app**
2. Hard refresh: **`Ctrl + Shift + R`**
3. **Farmer** → **Report Incident** → **Submit**
4. You should see **“Report Submitted Successfully”**

First API call may take **30–60 seconds** (Render waking up) — wait, then try again.

---

**Yes — you need to redeploy** if you added or changed `VITE_API_BASE_URL`.

### Why
Vite bakes env vars into the build at **deploy time**. Saving the variable alone does **not** update the live site.

### When to redeploy

| Situation | Redeploy? |
|-----------|-----------|
| Just added/changed `VITE_API_BASE_URL` | **Yes** ✅ |
| Only changed Render CORS | **No** (Render redeploys itself) |
| Already redeployed **after** setting the env var | **No** |

### What to do
1. Vercel → **backend-farm** → **Deployments**
2. **⋯** → **Redeploy**
3. **Clear build cache** → **ON**
4. **Redeploy**
5. Wait until **Ready**, then test submit

**Short answer:** set env var → **redeploy once** → test.
